text:
maya-support: FYI customer Skylark hit mid-stream disconnects when their iOS app goes to background. They get a few partial chunks (gzip) then stream stops. Billing charged full generation. conn=c-9f4b2a region=us-west-2 app=v2.3.1 iOS=17.2
ivan-engineering: Can you paste the correlation id + raw headers from the failed request and the app-side console logs? Also include whether this is SSE or chunked HTTP streaming.
alex-mobile: It's SSE. Quick repro steps I used on a test device: background the app for ~12s while streaming a long reply. Observed server keepalive then no more data after a partial gzipped chunk. I can reproduce consistently on iPhone 14.
alex-mobile: Reproducer (curl):

curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -H "Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate" "https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream?model=gpt-xl"

Response shows initial events, then a chunk like:

data: {"id":"msg-abc","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Good afternoon, here
"}}]}
[data flush - gzipped]

then nothing, socket stays open on client for ~30s then closes. Server logs show 200 until idle timeout.
ivan-engineering: Hmm. Two hypotheses: (1) edge gzip buffering + chunk flush boundary is causing the client to see incomplete decompression after suspend/resume, (2) proxy idle timeout doesn't propagate TLS close so app thinks stream is alive. Can you try sending `Accept-Encoding: identity` and see if this prevents the issue?
alex-mobile: Tried that — when I force `Accept-Encoding: identity` the stream survives background/resume and we get full output. So seems tied to gzip/chunk flush semantics.
julie-cs: Customer wants a refund for the failed run (they were billed). Marked P1. They can repro and will share device logs if eng needs them.
sre-bot: [ALERT] stream-silence spike detected in us-west-2 (last 15m) — 18 occurrences, median silence 14s.
ivan-engineering: Thanks. I'll loop in eng-runtime and eng-sre. Action items: (1) eng-runtime: investigate gzip chunking behavior for SSE (disable gzip for SSE endpoints or ensure flush semantics), (2) eng-sre / edge: check proxy idle timeouts and proper TCP/TLS close propagation, (3) billing: whitelist first failed token charge pending refund decision.
ivan-engineering: Quick diagnostic suggestion: reproduce with tcpdump on device or proxy to see whether compressed chunk is incomplete at TCP layer or it's post-decompress issue. Also check response headers `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` vs `Content-Length` mismatch.
maya-support: Customer will provide app console + Xcode network logs and a sample correlation id c-9f4b2a. I'll attach when they send.
alex-mobile: Additional note: toggling `Accept-Encoding` on the SDK side is an easy workaround — we can push a hotfix to set `Accept-Encoding: identity` for SSE streams until runtime fix.
julie-cs: I'll draft the refund note and let billing know to pause charging for the session while we investigate.
ivan-engineering: Assigning owners: eng-runtime @ivan-engineering (triage EOD), eng-sre @sre-oncall (investigate edge config, 24h), SDK hotfix @alex-mobile (eta next patch). Support to collect logs @maya-support.
maya-support: Thanks — will relay and follow up once we have device logs. :eyes: :white_check_mark:
